description:
BenchBox currently prints "Running {benchmark} on {platform} at scale {scale}" before
resolving the database config, so the driver version isn't known at that point. Users
have no visible indication of which driver version actually ran until they inspect the
result JSON.

This became a concrete UX problem: a user manually installed duckdb==1.5.0.dev307 via
uv pip install, then ran benchbox without specifying --platform-option driver_version=X.
uv run silently reverted the package to the uv.lock-pinned 1.4.3 before Python started.
The result JSON correctly reported 1.4.3, but the user only discovered the discrepancy
by reading the result file - never from the CLI output.

The fix is to emit driver version after config resolution, either by:
  a) Moving the "Running ..." line to after database_config is created (line 1402 in
     commands/run.py), so version is available to include inline.
  b) Adding a second, briefer line like "  ↳ driver: duckdb 1.4.3 (current-process)"
     immediately after config creation.

The preferred output is option (a): one combined line.
Target format: "Running {benchmark} on {platform} at scale {scale} [driver {version}]"
Example: "Running clickbench on duckdb at scale 10.0 [driver 1.4.3]"

For platforms where no version was explicitly requested (the common case), still show
the actual resolved version so the user can see what's running. For platforms without
a driver package (e.g., SQLite), omit the driver clause.
